name: Mohammed V International Airport
before:
Morocco's busiest airport and one of the ten busiest in Africa, in Nouaceur Province, serving Casablanca. It is the hub for Royal Air Maroc, Royal Air Maroc Express and Air Arabia Maroc, and handled around 7.6 million passengers in 2022.

The train is the easy way in and out. The Al Bidaoui service is run by ONCF every hour from four in the morning until eleven at night and reaches both of Casablanca's main stations, Casa-Port and Casa-Voyageurs. By road the A3 runs from Casablanca and from Marrakesh, and the A1 from Rabat and El Jadida.

The airport was built by the United States in early 1943, after Operation Torch, as Berrechid Airfield. It worked as an auxiliary field for Anfa Airport in Casablanca, a stop on the Cairo to Dakar route across North Africa and the terminus of transatlantic flights running by way of the Azores to Nova Scotia. It was handed over for civil use in 1945.

It is named after King Mohammed V.
after: Morocco's busiest airport, serving Casablanca from about 20 to 25 km south of the city centre in a straight line. It is the hub for Royal Air Maroc, and Royal Air Maroc Express flies domestic routes from here.

claims.note: Busiest by passengers. ONDA's figures for the first half of 2026, as Morocco World News reported them on 16 July 2026, put Mohammed V first with 5,756,388 passengers, narrowly ahead of Marrakech Menara with 5,636,776. Wikipedia says it was the busiest in 2022. Hespress (6 September 2026, citing ONDA) has nearly 6.95 million at Mohammed V in the first seven months of 2026, against 22.28 million at all Moroccan airports.

claims.claim: one of the ten busiest in Africa
claims.wasBefore: and one of the ten busiest in Africa
claims.why: A 2022 ranking (Wikipedia: fourth in Africa in 2022, citing Hespress). No ranking from the last 12 months could be read, so it is not repeated.

Wikipedia alone. The airport's own site (aeroportcasablanca.ma) shows Cloudflare's 'Just a moment... Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue' check and ONDA's (onda.ma) is behind Cloudflare too, so no address could be read. The text gives the airport's position from two coordinate sets instead (above).

claims.claim: the hub for Royal Air Maroc Express and Air Arabia Maroc
claims.wasBefore: Royal Air Maroc Express and Air Arabia Maroc
claims.why: Royal Air Maroc Express is softened to flying domestic routes from here (above). Air Arabia Maroc rests on Wikipedia alone: airarabia.com refused the link lister (403), so it was not fetched with any other tool, and Hespress's Air Arabia index has no report from the last 12 months of Air Arabia Maroc flying from Casablanca.

claims.wasBefore: and handled around 7.6 million passengers in 2022
claims.why: Four years old, and no newer figure has two sources of its own. ONDA, which publishes the figures, is behind Cloudflare. Wikipedia's infobox gives 10,449,372 for 2024 (citing France Aviation Civile Services, whose April 2026 bulletin page carries no figures as text). No full-year 2025 figure for Mohammed V was found in the indexes of Morocco World News or Hespress English, and MAP's English site refused the link lister (403). The 2026 figures found each rest on one outlet reporting ONDA: 5,756,388 in the first half, up 10.13 per cent (Morocco World News, 16 July 2026), and nearly 6.95 million in the first seven months, up 9.7 per cent (Hespress, 6 September 2026). 'Morocco's busiest airport' is kept (above). A current total can go back when a second source for the same period is found.

sources.quote: Mohammed V International Airport recorded the highest passenger volume, with 5,756,388 travelers, marking a 10.13% increase compared with the first six months of 2025.

quote: Casablanca’s Mohammed V International Airport handled nearly 6.95 million passengers during the first seven months of 2026, up 9.7% from 6.34 million a year earlier, Morocco’s National Airports Office said.

claims.claim: the Al Bidaoui train, run by ONCF hourly from 04:00 to 23:00, to Casa-Port and Casa-Voyageurs
claims.wasBefore: The train is the easy way in and out. The Al Bidaoui service is run by ONCF every hour from four in the morning until eleven at night and reaches both of Casablanca's main stations, Casa-Port and Casa-Voyageurs.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. ONCF's two sites (oncf.ma and oncf-voyages.ma) each answered 502 to one try; Hespress's and Morocco World News's ONCF indexes, Hespress's July 2026 report on Casablanca's new regional rail stations and Visit Morocco's getting-around page say nothing about the airport train. The biggest practical loss in this text: restore it when ONCF's timetable can be read.

claims.claim: UK routes in 2025: Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester and Stansted
claims.why: Held back: a new fact that replaces nothing. The UK CAA's 2025 table counts passengers between Casablanca and Heathrow (112,043, down 11.8 per cent), Gatwick (78,893), Manchester (32,857, more than double 2024's 15,712) and Stansted (11,338, none in 2024). No saved page names the airline on each UK route.

claims.claim: a new terminal for 2029, a new parallel runway and a high-speed rail station
claims.why: Held back: a new fact that replaces nothing, and on Wikipedia alone. Wikipedia says ONDA put a new H-shaped terminal out to tender in May 2025 (about US$1.6 billion, capacity from about 15 to 35 million a year, due by 2029 for the 2030 World Cup), with a new parallel runway, a new control tower and a high-speed rail station, and that earthworks began in mid-2025. Its source, Reuters, is blocked by the session's egress policy (one try, not retried), and nothing from the last 12 months was found. Works at the airport may matter to travellers, so worth checking by hand.

quote: In May 2025 Morocco's airports authority Moroccan Airports Authority launched an international tender to build a new H-shaped terminal at Mohammed V International Airport
is expected to be completed by 2029 in time for the 2030 FIFA World Cup
Earthworks began in mid-2025 with main construction slated to follow and full operation targeted for 2029.
